item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 271718
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Mon Jul 27 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Fausto, located in the Central Pacific several hundred miles east of
the Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Genevieve, located several
hundred miles south-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Papin

item.description: ...MAJOR HURRICANE GENEVIEVE CONTINUES NORTHWESTWARD... As of 2:00 PM MST Mon Jul 27 the center of Genevieve was located near 16.6, -113.9 with movement NW at 13 mph. The minimum central pressure was 934 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 150 mph.

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Public Advisory Number 14
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Mon Jul 27 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 272048
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Genevieve Advisory Number  14
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
200 PM MST Mon Jul 27 2026
 
...MAJOR HURRICANE GENEVIEVE CONTINUES NORTHWESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.6N 113.9W
ABOUT 505 MI...815 KM SSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...150 MPH...240 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 13 MPH...20 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...934 MB...27.58 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Genevieve was 
located near latitude 16.6 North, longitude 113.9 West. Genevieve is 
moving toward the northwest near 13 mph (20 km/h). A 
west-northwestward to northwestward motion with some decrease in 
forward speed is expected during the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 150 mph (240 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Genevieve is a category 4 hurricane on the 
Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale.  Some fluctuations in intensity 
are possible this afternoon, but steady weakening is forecast to 
begin by tonight through the remainder of the week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 934 mb (27.58 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Genevieve are affecting portions of the
southwestern coast of Mexico and southern portions of the Baja
California Peninsula, and will spread northward along the remainder
of the west coast of the Baja California Peninsula by tonight. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams/Papin

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Forecast Discussion Number 14
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Mon Jul 27 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 272050
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Genevieve Discussion Number  14
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
200 PM MST Mon Jul 27 2026
 
After some warming of the eyewall cloud top temperatures this 
morning, the infrared satellite presentation of Major Hurricane 
Genevieve has improved over the past couple of hours, with colder 
cloud tops wrapping around the western side of the clear, symmetric, 
and very warm eye. It is possible Genevieve could soon undergo an 
eyewall replacement cycle, though there have been no recent 
microwave images to definitively determine whether one is underway. 
The latest subjective intensity estimates range from 120-130 kt, 
with the 1800 UTC estimate from TAFB at 6.5/127 kt. The initial 
intensity has been set at 130 kt for this advisory. 

The hurricane is being steered by a strong mid-level ridge centered 
over the central United States, and is moving toward the northwest 
around 310/11 kt. Genevieve is forecast to slow down slightly over 
the next 48 h or so as the ridge weakens and progresses eastward. A 
faster west-northwestward motion is expected late this week into 
this weekend as a mid-level ridge builds to the northwest of the 
cyclone. The latest NHC track forecast is very similar to the 
previous advisory and lies near the HCCA corrected consensus.

Colder cloud tops surrounding the eye indicate some fluctuations in 
intensity could occur with Genevieve this afternoon. However, as the 
hurricane moves toward the northwest and west-northwest this week, a 
steady weakening trend is expected as it encounters cooler waters 
and gradually drier mid-level relative humidity. By early Thursday, 
Genevieve is forecast to move north of 20N and encounter waters 
cooler than 26 C, leading to a faster weakening trend for late this 
week into this weekend. The latest NHC forecast calls for Genevieve 
to become post-tropical by 120 h, and this is consistent with 
current model guidance.
